title: The Midnight Wolf
premise: Marguerite Whitlock has spent twelve years hiding her gift behind harmless charms in Greyhollow, a city where magic was outlawed after the Sundering War. When the crown's witch-hunters arrive and begin burning the last guild members one by one, Marguerite discovers she carries something far more dangerous than a talent: the sealed memories of the Wolf of Winter, the ancient guardian whose sacrifice ended the war—and whose return the old bloodlines have been waiting for. Hunted by Inquisitor Corvane, a man who once loved her mother, Marguerite finds refuge with a ragtag found family of smugglers, exiles, and a fellow survivor named Tomas who remembers her from a life she never lived. As the long winter falls and her stolen memories surface, she must choose between erasing herself forever to keep the peace or awakening as the Wolf and risking a war that could consume everything she loves. In the end, she forges a third path: she shares the memory among her found family, breaking the cycle of solitary guardianship and proving that identity need not be carried alone.
about_author: Ada Dunmore is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing folk charms in northern England before turning to fiction. She writes quiet, wintry fantasy about people who survive by being overlooked.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. On market day in Greyhollow, she sells luck-knots and fever-charms to neighbors who half-suspect but never ask. She tends the crumbling guildhall where her mentor Odile sleeps more each day. The beat is quiet longing: a life built on smallness, and the ache of pretending it's enough.

chapters.title: The Proclamation
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Criers announce the crown's Edict of Ash: all gifted persons must register within thirty days or be hunted. A neighbor she's charmed for years looks at her differently. Marguerite burns her ledger and warns Odile, who only says, 'It found us anyway.' Beat: dread settling into bone.

chapters.title: What Odile Kept
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Searching the guildhall for escape routes, Marguerite finds a locked box containing a wolf-tooth pendant and a letter naming her—not as apprentice, but as vessel. Odile confesses fragments: the gift Marguerite carries isn't hers. Beat: betrayal braided with fierce protectiveness.

chapters.title: The First Fire
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. A smuggler who runs river goods past the city walls, Tomas watches witch-smoke rise over the tanner's quarter and recognizes the victim: a hedge-witch who once healed his sister. He decides to start moving the gifted out. Beat: grief hardening into purpose.

chapters.title: Inquisitor Corvane
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The crown's chief hunter interrogates a registered charm-maker and lets him go—because he's building a map, not making arrests. He studies an old portrait of Elara Whitlock, Marguerite's mother, and murmurs that the daughter will be harder. Beat: patient menace; the hunter who grieves what he hunts.

chapters.title: The River Road
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Marguerite flees Greyhollow with Odile too frail to travel far; they leave her hidden with a herbalist. On the river road, smugglers become reluctant allies. Marguerite lies about what she is; Tomas pretends to believe her. Beat: wary trust kindling between strangers.

chapters.title: Memories Not Mine
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Fevered in a smuggler's safehouse, Marguerite dreams in another woman's voice: snowfields, a wolf made of winter, a sealing ritual gone wrong. She wakes with frost on her palms in midsummer. Beat: terror of a self bleeding through the seams.

chapters.title: The Company of Strays
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The safehouse gathers its odd family: Sefa, a disgraced battle-mage; Pip, a child who speaks to locks; Bramble, a shapeshifter stuck half-fox. They argue, share supper, and name themselves nothing at all. Beat: warmth discovered inside danger—the found family taking shape.

chapters.title: Corvane Closes
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. His map fills; he traces the smuggling route to the safehouse district and offers amnesty to informants. A flashback reveals his history with Elara Whitlock: they were friends before the Edict made them enemies on opposite sides of a secret. Beat: sorrow weaponized into duty.

chapters.title: The Raid
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Hunters hit the safehouse at dawn. Sefa holds a doorway with raw force; Pip unlocks a cellar no one knew existed. They escape through the sewers, but Bramble is taken. Marguerite's frost flares publicly for the first time. Beat: the cost of staying together.

chapters.title: What the Fox Confessed
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Interrogating Bramble, Corvane learns of the vessel and the Wolf of Winter. He doesn't torture the shapeshifter—he offers tea and truth, which is worse. Bramble gives up nothing but a riddle. Beat: the inquisitor's certainty beginning to crack.

chapters.title: Odile's Last Lesson
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Reaching the herbalist's cottage, Marguerite finds Odile dying. With her final strength, Odile performs a partial unsealing: Marguerite sees the whole war, the Wolf's willing sacrifice, and her mother's role in hiding the memory inside a newborn daughter. Beat: devastating clarity; identity rewritten.

chapters.title: The Long Winter Falls
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Snow arrives early and wrong—unnatural, responding to the unsealing like a tide to a moon. Rivers freeze; the hunt becomes a siege. Tomas realizes Marguerite isn't cargo to protect but the storm itself. Beat: awe and fear reshaping loyalty into devotion.

chapters.title: The Crown's Bargain
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. The old bloodlines at court reveal their true aim: not eradicating magic but claiming the Wolf's power for the throne. Corvane is ordered to bring the vessel alive. He asks what happens to the girl inside. No one answers. Beat: the loyal servant seeing the rot above him.

chapters.title: Wolfkin
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Training with Sefa, Marguerite stops fighting the memories and begins conversing with them—the Wolf was a person once, lonely as she is. Her power stabilizes when she accepts rather than resists. Beat: tentative reconciliation with the self she didn't choose.

chapters.title: The Rescue at Ashgate
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. The company raids Ashgate Prison to free Bramble and the captured gifted. Pip picks the impossible lock; Sefa burns the ledgers of names. They leave the cells open for everyone. Beat: triumphant solidarity—the family choosing risk over safety, together.

chapters.title: Corvane's Choice
chapters.summary: Corvane's POV. Ordered to burn Ashgate's survivors as an example, Corvane instead releases his prisoners' list to the wind and resigns his commission—or tries to. The bloodlines mark him for death. He rides north, toward the very woman he hunted. Beat: defection born of conscience.

chapters.title: The Siege of Greyhollow
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. The crown's army surrounds the city where her story began, demanding the vessel. Marguerite walks the walls among refugees from every raid and realizes the war they fear already lives in every heart that hoards power. Beat: resolve crystallizing into a third option.

chapters.title: The Unmaking Offered
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. At the guildhall ruins, the bloodlines' sorcerer offers her oblivion: erase the Wolf, erase the war, erase herself. Marguerite nearly accepts—twelve years of invisibility whispering that smallness is safety. Tomas's voice calls her back to her own name. Beat: the darkest hour, temptation of self-erasure.

chapters.title: Winter Remembers
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Climax. Instead of destroying the memory or keeping it, Marguerite opens the seal and shares the Wolf across everyone willing to hold a piece—Sefa, Pip, Bramble, Tomas, even Corvane. Power distributed cannot be crowned or burned. The sorcerer's claim collapses; the army falters in a snowfall that feels, for once, like blessing. Beat: transcendence through shared burden.

chapters.title: After the Thaw
chapters.summary: Tomas's POV. Weeks later: the Edict is suspended, the guildhall reopens with new names on its door, and magic returns cautiously to daylight. Corvane plants a garden over the ash-pits. Marguerite sells charms again—but now they're just charms, and she is just herself, multiplied. Beat: tender, earned peace.

chapters.title: The Names on the Door
chapters.summary: Marguerite's POV. Epilogue. On midwinter night, the found family gathers to carve their names beside the guild founders'. Marguerite adds one more beneath them: the Wolf's true name, remembered at last by many instead of buried in one. Beat: belonging; identity as a thing held in common, going forward.
